title: Text file busy - cannot overwrite a program that is running
summary: Linux does not let you replace a program file while the program is running, and cp shows this as 'Text file busy'. Stop the program first, then copy the new file.

prerequisites: The path of the file named in the error message

steps.explain: Find the running copy of the program. Use the path from the error message. The first number on each line is the process ID (PID) you need in the next steps.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_PATH
placeholders.description: Path of the program file the error message names

steps.expect: A line like '12 /tmp/busy': the number is the PID. No output means nothing runs from that path, so the file is not the cause.

steps.explain: Stop the running program. Save your work in it first. Replace <PID> with the number from the previous step.

placeholders.name: PID
placeholders.description: Process number from the first column of the previous step

steps.expect: No output. The program closes. Running the first command again prints nothing.

alternatives.explain: If the program does not close, force it to quit. Unsaved work in it will be lost.

placeholders.name: PID
placeholders.description: Process number from the first step

alternatives.expect: No output. The program is stopped.

steps.explain: Keep a backup copy of the old program file, in case you need to go back.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_PATH
placeholders.description: Path of the program file being replaced

steps.expect: No output. A file ending in .bak appears next to the program.

steps.explain: Copy the new version of the program over the old file.

placeholders.name: NEW_FILE
placeholders.description: Path to the new version of the program

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_PATH
placeholders.description: Path of the program file being replaced

steps.expect: No output when the copy works. If the program is still running, the 'Text file busy' error appears again.

alternatives.explain: Delete the old file and copy the new one in one command. This works even while the old program still runs; the running copy keeps working until it is closed.

placeholders.name: NEW_FILE
placeholders.description: Path to the new version of the program

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_PATH
placeholders.description: Path of the program file being replaced

alternatives.expect: No output. The file is replaced.

verify.expect: No output: the new file and the installed program are identical.

rollback.explain: Put the backup copy back over the new file. Stop the new program first, as in the kill step.

placeholders.name: PROGRAM_PATH
placeholders.description: Path of the program file that was replaced

warnings: Killing a program can lose unsaved work. Save your files before you stop it.
Only copy a new program file that you trust and that is built for your system.
Do not replace programs in system folders such as /usr or /bin by hand unless you know what you are doing.
